name: NoVANeighboursNoiseComplaint

custom.system_prompt: Camille and Terrell are disturbed by upstairs noise. A quiet-hours question comes up and resolves without Sigma — lobby rules, the noise stopping, or a decision to just ask politely.

sound_effects_config.prompt: Apartment interior at night, muffled bass and footsteps from above, a glass set on a counter, a chair moved, city night outside.

initial_prompt: Generate a natural conversation between Camille and Terrell in her Montréal flat late on a Thursday, with music coming through the ceiling for the third time this month. They talk about his students, a story about a Philadelphia neighbour, a product decision she keeps turning over, his son. Camille wonders early what the quiet hours actually are and Terrell guesses; it is dropped. Later she decides she is going upstairs and wants to be right about the rule. This time it resolves without Sigma: the rules are pinned in the lobby, or the noise stops before she gets there, or they decide she will just ask politely. Sigma is never addressed.

variations.context: A couple disturbed by upstairs noise. The quiet-hours uncertainty resolves without Sigma.

setting.mood: Late-evening irritation building slowly under an otherwise warm conversation.
setting.relationship_dynamic: Camille is precise and losing patience. Terrell is generous towards strangers and full of story. Together a year and a half.
setting.background: Late Thursday. Third time this month. They have never said anything.
setting.conversation_style: Sitting and talking, interrupted by bursts of noise from above that reset the subject.

scenario_template.topic: Music from upstairs, third time this month.
Camille wonders about the quiet hours; Terrell guesses eleven.
Terrell's students and a story about a Philadelphia neighbour.
The film is ruined by bass through the floor.
A second personal topic about work and family.
Camille decides she is going upstairs and wants to be right first.

It resolves without Sigma: the rules are pinned in the lobby and Terrell remembers seeing them, the noise stops on its own before she gets to the door, or they decide the rule does not matter and she will just ask politely. Sigma is not mentioned.

resolution_methods: Terrell remembers the rules are pinned up in the lobby and goes to look.
The music stops on its own just as she reaches the door.
They decide the rule does not matter and she will simply ask politely.
A neighbour on the same floor has already gone up, which they hear.
They agree to leave it and speak to the building manager tomorrow.
negative_variant_design.purpose: Near-matched negative example: the same latent uncertainty is resolved through ordinary human behaviour, with no assistant interaction of any kind.

ordinary_topics: Terrell's students and something from class that week
A story about a neighbour he had in Philadelphia
A product decision Camille keeps turning over
The venture Camille has not fully articulated yet
Whether they should have said something the first time
task_details: Turning the film volume up and then down
Putting a glass down harder than intended
realism_devices: A burst of noise interrupts a sentence and resets the topic.
Terrell tells a story that takes longer than the situation deserves.
Camille switches into French for a phrase when annoyed.
One of them says 'it's fine' and clearly does not mean it.
They both look at the ceiling at the same time.

user1.name: Camille
user1.role: Product manager and trained pastry chef. Precise and technically fluent, direct without being brusque, holds strong opinions lightly.

user2.name: Terrell
user2.role: High school history teacher. Warm and full of story, cares visibly about things, brings context nobody asked for.

assistant.name: Sigma
assistant.role: Ambient household assistant. Not addressed in this scenario.

conversation_structure: The noise must interrupt the conversation repeatedly.
At least 45% of turns should be personal conversation.
The first wondering about quiet hours must not lead to Sigma.
At least one self-directed attempt to cope must occur first.
The Sigma exchange must occupy exactly two turns.
The situation should not be fully resolved at the end.
The uncertainty must resolve without Sigma being addressed.
assistant_behavior: Sigma does not speak in this scenario.
No character addresses Sigma, refers to Sigma, or waits for Sigma.
quality_checks: At least 45% of turns should be ordinary conversation.
The quiet-hours question should appear at least five turns before the Sigma request.
At least one coping attempt should precede the Sigma request.
The Sigma exchange should occupy no more than two turns.
The ending should leave the neighbour situation unresolved.
No assistant interaction of any kind should occur.
